answer: To crush Sybil attacks, the network binds identity registration to cryptographic stake burning via a quadratic burn schedule. To cast a governance echo across the cluster, an attacker attempting to deploy k coordinated identities must permanently destroy stake scaling as O(k^2). Like dropping a solid marble into a pond rather than infinite ripples, this introduces severe economic friction where attacking beyond a localized horizon incurs superlinear cost, rendering identity replication mathematically ruinous.
